description: ASHRAE Standard 140, the Method of Test for Evaluating Building Performance Simulation Software, specifies test procedures to assess the technical capabilities and range of application of software that simulates buildings and their systems, and its test suites grew out of the BESTEST work. The method is designed to identify and diagnose differences between programs caused by algorithms, modelling limits, coding faults, documentation or input errors, testing over many parametric interactions and output types so that compensating errors do not hide differences. The ASHRAE site hosts supporting material: accompanying electronic files to be used with the standard, reference files on the standard and its committee, and analysis files for comparing results from the test cases. Coverage: test cases for whole building and system simulation software. Access: downloads from data.ashrae.org. Licence: ASHRAE terms; the supporting files are free while the standard is purchased. Caveats: the tests reveal major flaws or limits but cannot test every algorithm, and some tests do not suit every program. Simulation uses are verifying building energy software and custom models before using them for studies, and comparing engines. Related records: EnergyPlus and the IEA EBC Annex 58 empirical validation data.
